representation.prompts: Native HTML and KaTeX for every prompt with original wording, part labels, marks, bold emphasis, question-specific instructions, tables and faithful vector figure crops. As in the earlier imports, printed captions such as "Figure 1" sit outside the crop and the figure is referred to by the original text.
representation.solutions: Every question-specific mark-scheme page as ordered vector crops: working, marks, AOs, alternatives, examiner notes and diagrams. The Sample Assessment Materials page footer (Pearson imprint and page-number box) is excluded.

cropMethod: PyMuPDF show_pdf_page clip to SVG with text as paths. Figure boxes were set from the drawing items and checked visually in Chrome. Scheme page bounds cover all text spans, vector drawings and embedded images above the footer band; breaks fall only in empty horizontal bands; drawing items lying wholly off the page are ignored.
sourceNotes: Files were identified by their covers, not their names; the full inventory (SHA-256, page counts, pairing, duplicates) is on GitHub #124 and the release slice on #128.
These are Sample Assessment Materials: session "Sample", no exam date and no series date (none invented). The Past Papers list places them after all dated papers, ordered by code.
June 2022 folder: all 12 files are byte-identical to Summer 2023 files imported in v0.69, so they are skipped; no genuine 2022 paper was supplied.

The question papers and the 9FM0/01 mark scheme have no readable PDF text layer (custom font encodings); prompts were transcribed from page images (OCR used only as an aid) and scheme crops are vector crops of the original pages.

Paper instructions are taken verbatim from each cover: "You should show sufficient working to make your methods clear. Answers without working may not gain full credit." and "Answers should be given to three significant figures unless otherwise stated." 9MA0/03 Q6-Q10 also carry the Section B: Mechanics instruction verbatim (g = 9.8 m s^-2, answers to 2 or 3 significant figures).
9MA0/03 is one combined paper with original numbering: Section A Statistics Q1-Q5 and Section B Mechanics Q6-Q10. Its question paper has 26 pages; page 26 is a blank back page.
9MA0/03 Q1 prints "5.98 hours and 4.12 hours respectably" (for "respectively"); it is kept verbatim and not corrected.
9MA0/03 Q10 and 9FM0/01 Q9 state their own g = 10 m s^-2 in the question text; it is kept in the question.
9MA0/02 Q6 is an always/sometimes/never-true table with marks in each statement row; it is reproduced as a table with the worked first row and blank answer cells.
Mid-page scheme starts (9MA0/01 Q4, 9MA0/02 Q2 and Q10) are cut above the question header row or label, so every question carries only its own scheme.
mathsReview: Every question solved independently with SymPy and numeric checks (private scripts) and compared with the official scheme answers; no mathematical discrepancies and no source errors found.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: Partial fractions and differences give n(5n + 13)/(12(n + 2)(n + 3)), a = 5, b = 13 (identity checked symbolically). Agrees with scheme.
f(1) = 391 = 17 x 23; f(k+1) - 8f(k) = 255 x 5^(2k) = 17 x 3 x 5^(2k+1), so divisibility passes from k to k+1 (f(n) mod 17 = 0 checked for n = 1..7). Agrees with scheme.
Conjugate 3 - 2i gives factor z^2 - 6z + 13; f(z) = (z^2 - 6z + 13)(z^2 + 2z + 5), roots 3 +/- 2i and -1 +/- 2i (a = -4, b = -4). Agrees with scheme.
r = 9/2 at theta = pi/6; sector area from 0 to pi/6 minus triangle ONA gives 11pi/8 - 3sqrt3/2, p = 11/8, q = -3/2. Agrees with scheme.
Volume 1000 + 5t, outflow 20x/(1000 + 5t), inflow 50 g/day give the ODE; with x(0) = 0 the solution gives x(8) = 370 g. Agrees with scheme.
Integral = (1/2)ln(x^2 + 9) + (2/3)arctan(x/3) + c; mean on [0, 3] = (1/6)ln2 + pi/18; adding ln k gives (pi/18) + (1/6)ln(2k^6). Agrees with scheme.
x^2 + y^4 + 2y^3 = 0 on the curve (checked numerically); V = pi times integral from -2 to 0 of -(y^4 + 2y^3) dy = 8pi/5 = 5.03 cm^3. Agrees with scheme.
l1 meets the plane at (10, 0, -4); the reflection of (2, 4, -6) is (8, -8, 0); l2: r = (10, 0, -4) + k(1, 4, -2). Agrees with scheme.
m = 30000/10/1000 = 3; 40 sin t - 20 cos t is a PI; with x(0) = 0, x'(0) = 0, x = 50e^-t - 30e^(-t/3) + 40 sin t - 20 cos t, x(9) = 33 m. Agrees with scheme.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: Sum 8, pair sum 28, product 32: (i) 28/32 = 7/8, (ii) 32 + 2(28) + 4(8) + 8 = 128, (iii) 8^2 - 2(28) = 8 (checked from numeric roots). Agrees with scheme.
Distance |18 - 8 + 24 - 5|/sqrt29 = sqrt29; (-1, -3, 1) is perpendicular to both direction vectors; acute angle between normals 51.98, i.e. 52 degrees. Agrees with scheme.
det M = 2(a + 5), so M is invertible for a != -5; M^-1 = adj(M)/(2a + 10) with adj rows (3, a+8, 4-a), (2, 2, 6), (1, -a-4, -a-2); matrix power formula checked for n = 1..7. Agrees with scheme.
z^n + z^-n = 2cos n theta; (z + 1/z)^4 expansion gives cos^4 theta = (cos 4theta + 4cos 2theta + 3)/8 (identity checked). Agrees with scheme.
y'''' = -4y; Maclaurin series x^2 - x^6/90 + x^10/113400; nth non-zero term 2(-4)^(n-1) x^(4n-2)/(4n-2)!. Agrees with scheme.
r = 8cos theta + 6sin theta is the circle |z - 4 - 3i| = 5; area of A = integral from 0 to pi/3 of r^2/2 = 25pi/3 + 18 + 7sqrt3/4. Agrees with scheme.

Eliminating r gives f'' - 0.6f' + 0.1f = 0, m = 0.3 +/- 0.1i; with f(0) = 6, r(0) = 20: f = e^(0.3t)(6cos 0.1t + 14sin 0.1t), r = e^(0.3t)(20cos 0.1t + 8sin 0.1t); r = 0 when tan 0.1t = -2.5, t = 19.5 (2019), f = 3750. Agrees with scheme.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: dy/dx = 12x^3 - 24x^2, d2y/dx2 = 36x^2 - 48x; at x = 2 dy/dx = 0 and d2y/dx2 = 48 > 0, a minimum. Agrees with scheme.
OD = 3/0.4 = 7.5 cm; AOB has radius 4.5 and angle pi - 0.4, area 27.8 cm^2. Agrees with scheme.
(x-2)^2 + (y+5)^2 = k + 29: centre (2, -5), k > -29. Agrees with scheme.
Integral of 1 + 1/t from a to 2a is a + ln 2 = ln 7, so a = ln(7/2), k = 7/2. Agrees with scheme.
t = (x+1)/2 gives y(x+1) = 2x^2 - 3x + 1, so a = -3, b = 1. Agrees with scheme.
Model A: V = 16000 - 1750t gives 10750 at t = 3; model B: V = 16000e^(-kt), k = ln(16/9)/4 = 0.1438, V(3) = 10400 (awrt). Agrees with scheme.
AC = AB + BC = 3i - 6j + 4k; cos BAC = AB.AC/(|AB||AC|) gives BAC = 105.9 degrees. Agrees with scheme.
f(3.5) = -4.81 < 0, f(4) = 3.10 > 0 (sign change); x1 = 4 - 3.099/16.67 = 3.81; f'(x) > 0 for x > 2.5 so f is increasing and alpha is the only root. Agrees with scheme.
tan + cot = 1/(sin cos) = 2/sin 2theta (identity checked numerically); = 1 would need sin 2theta = 2, impossible. Agrees with scheme.
Limit of (sin(theta+h) - sin theta)/h as h -> 0 is cos theta. Agrees with scheme.
H = 0 at d = 204 m (positive root); 1.8 is the launch height; H = 21.8 - 0.002(d - 100)^2; adapted max 22.1 m at d = 100 m. Agrees with scheme.
log N = log a + b log T so m = b, c = log a; reading a = 10^1.8 (about 63), b = 2.3 gives N(3) about 800 (scheme allows 800 +/- 150). Agrees with scheme.
dy/dx = 2 sqrt3 cos t; P = (-1, -sqrt3/2), normal 2x - 2sqrt3 y - 1 = 0 checked; second intersection Q = (5/3, 7sqrt3/18). Agrees with scheme.
Trapezium rule gives 4.393; exact area 28/27 + ln 27 (a = 28, b = 27, c = 27). Agrees with scheme.
f'(x) = 0 when 8cos2x = 4sqrt2 sin2x, i.e. tan 2x = sqrt2; P at x = 0.478, Q at x = 2.05; y = f(2x) minimum at x = 1.02; y = 3 - 2f(x) minimum at P, x = 0.478. Agrees with scheme.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: f(-2) = 0 gives -16 - 20 - 2a + a = 0, a = -36. Agrees with scheme.
Student A should have tan theta = 1/2; cos(-26.6) = 0.894 but 2sin(-26.6) = -0.896, so -26.6 is not a solution and arose from squaring. Agrees with scheme.
dy/dx = (2x+1)^3(10x+1): n = 3, A = 10, B = 1. Agrees with scheme.
gf(x) = 3x, fg(x) = x^3; x^3 = 3x with x > 0 has the single root sqrt3. Agrees with scheme.
m(0.5) = 25e^-0.025 = 24.4 g; dm/dt = -0.05m, k = -0.05. Agrees with scheme.
(i) (x-3)^2 + 1 > 0 always true; (ii) sometimes true (fails for a < 0); (iii) (n+1)^2 - n^2 = 2n + 1, always true. Agrees with scheme.
sqrt(4-x) = 2 - x/4 - x^2/64 + ..., k = -1/64; valid for |x| < 4 so x = 1 is valid. Agrees with scheme.
A = (0, 2), B = (5, 0); AD perpendicular to AB gives 2y - 5x = 4, D = (-0.8, 0); area = |AB||AD| = 11.6. Agrees with scheme.
Integral = 14 + 3A = 2A^2 gives A = -2 or 7/2 (discriminant 121 > 0). Agrees with scheme.
1 = (8/7)(1 - r^6) gives r^6 = 1/8, r = +/- 1/sqrt2, k = 2. Agrees with scheme.
Range f(x) >= 5; f(x) = x/2 + 30 gives x = 62/3 only; two roots for 5 < k <= 11. Agrees with scheme.
12 sin^2 x + sin x - 1 = 0: sin x = 1/4 or -1/3, x = 14.48, 165.52, -19.47, -160.53; (b) 2theta - 30 = -19.47 gives theta = 5.26. Agrees with scheme.
R = sqrt109, alpha = 16.70; a = 11, H = 11 - sqrt109 cos(80t + 16.70), max 21.44 m; second max at 80t + 16.70 = 540, t = 6.54 min = 6 min 32 s. Agrees with scheme.
pi r^2 h = 500 gives S = 2 pi r^2 + 1000/r; dS/dr = 0 gives r = 4.30 cm, h = 8.60 cm. Agrees with scheme.
dy/dx at x = 4 is 6, tangent y = 6x - 9; area of R = integral from 0 to 4 of (C - l) = 24. Agrees with scheme.
1/(P(11-2P)) = 1/(11P) + 2/(11(11-2P)); P(t) = 11/(2 + 9e^(-t/2)) satisfies the ODE with P(0) = 1 (A = 11, B = 2, C = 9); P = 2 at t = 2 ln(18/7) = 1.89 years. Agrees with scheme.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: Frequency density scale gives width 2.5 cm and height 7.2 cm; mean 6.63 and sd 3.69 (3 s.f.); about 7 days above mean + sd (interpolation); N(6.6, 3.7^2) predicts 31 x 0.1587 = 4.9 days. Agrees with scheme.
Critical value for n = 9 at 5% one-tail is 0.5822; r = 0.609 > 0.5822 so reject H0. Agrees with scheme.
P(tray >= 15) = 0.299 under B(24, 0.55); P(T >= 5) for T ~ B(10, 0.299) = 0.149; normal approximation N(132, 59.4) with continuity gives P(X >= 149.5) = 0.0116. Agrees with scheme.
v = (20 + 2.5t^2) i - 10t^(3/2) j; v(4) = 60i - 80j, speed 100 m/s. Agrees with scheme.
Deceleration g(sin a + mu cos a) = 4g/5 with sin a = 3/5, cos a = 4/5 gives mu = 1/4; mu < tan a = 3/4 so the particle slides back down. Agrees with scheme.

a = ((10.5i - 0.9j) - 0.6j)/15 = 0.7i - 0.1j; r = 0.35t^2 i + (0.6t - 0.05t^2) j; north-east of O when components equal, t = 1.5; moving north-east when velocity components equal, t = 0.75. Agrees with scheme.
Moments about A with tan a = 5/2 give S = 3W; R = 8W, F max = 2W, so W <= P <= 5W. Agrees with scheme.
36 = (4U/5)T and -18 = (3U/5)T - 5T^2 give T = 3, U = 15; at 10.8 m above sea level (7.2 m below O) speed = sqrt(225 + 144) = 19 m/s (2 s.f.). Agrees with scheme.
